text: Both ends of the eclipse axis run the show at once here. Your long chapter belongs to Rahu, the Moon's north node, the point of appetite and outward reach. Inside it runs a shorter period, an antardasha, ruled by Ketu, the south node, which pulls the other way toward release and quiet. The mixture is genuinely odd, and many people feel it as a stall. You still want the big thing, and some part of you has stopped believing in it. Effort that paid last year can pay less now, and a prize you chased hard can go flat once it is in your hands. That flatness is worth reading rather than arguing with. This stretch tends to sort the hungers that are actually yours from the ones you caught from other people. Some ambitions drop off the list here and are never missed. Others survive the doubt and come back with better reasons attached. Work can turn inward for a while: research, repair, finishing, tidying what the earlier push left in a mess. Threads from before this chapter may resurface, sometimes to close, sometimes to be picked up again. Travel and withdrawal can both appeal, and either can serve. Restlessness without a target is the usual complaint, so solitude tends to do more for you here than another plan would. What you carry out of it is a shorter list of wants, held with less noise around them.

Desire meets taste in this stretch. Your present chapter belongs to Rahu, the north node of the Moon, a point the tradition reads as hunger rather than as a planet. Each such chapter divides again, and the divisions have a name, antardasha, meaning a period inside the period. Venus runs this one, so the hunger of the era turns toward people, pleasure, beauty, and comfort. Relationships often get interesting now, in both senses of the word. Attractions can arrive from well outside your usual circle: someone from another country, another background, another world entirely, and the pull tends to be strong and hard to explain to friends. Some of these bonds become the making of a life. Others turn out to be the appetite wearing a lovely face. Telling them apart usually takes time, which this pairing is reluctant to give. Money and possessions can climb the agenda too. Spending may run warmer than planned, taste may outgrow the budget, and beautiful objects can start standing in for a feeling you have not named. Creative work tends to do well here, especially anything with an audience and a little glamour attached. Nothing is decided by this combination. It raises the volume of wanting and puts an appealing surface on it, which is why enjoyment and honesty both have to be chosen on purpose. Chosen that way, it can be one of the more delightful runs inside a demanding chapter, and you finish it knowing your own taste better.

Ambition acquires a face here. Your long chapter runs under Rahu. That is the Moon's north node, and it leans toward reach beyond where you started. Within such a chapter every lord gets a turn of its own, called an antardasha or sub-period, and the Sun's turn brings identity, authority, and visibility into the mix. Recognition becomes a live issue rather than an afterthought. You may be seen more, at work or in public, and what people see may not match what you feel from the inside. Some readers step up in title or standing during this run. Others feel the gap between the position they hold and the one they had pictured. Both versions ask the same question, which is whose approval you are working for. Bosses, officials, and anyone who signs off on your work tend to loom larger, and a father or whoever stood for authority early on can come forward in the story as well. Pride runs high, and so can the temptation to claim a bit more than the record supports, since this chapter is always happy to help with the packaging. The steadier route is unglamorous: let the work be visible and let credit arrive at its own pace. Health and plain energy deserve attention too, because ambition spends both without asking first. Used well, the pairing turns raw wanting into something that carries your name, and shows you firsthand how you behave when people are watching.

The feeling life gets drawn into the ambition. Rahu governs the long chapter you are in. Rahu is the Moon's north node, and its habit is to enlarge whatever you want. A shorter period inside that chapter, called an antardasha, hands the tone to a single lord for a while, and this one belongs to the Moon: home, mood, memory, and care. The combination is restless. Your inner weather shifts faster than usual, and the wanting that drives the era starts showing up in your sleep, your appetite, and your imagination at two in the morning. Moves are common now in the literal sense, a new house, a new city, a household rearranged around a plan. Family may be part of the reaching, either as support or as what gets left behind for a season. A mother, or whoever did the mothering, often appears in the story of this run. Public feeling matters too. If your work touches an audience, response can be warm and quick here, though it moves like water and should not be mistaken for ground. The trap is deciding at high tide or low tide instead of somewhere in between, since a mood can dress itself up convincingly as a strategy. Anything that returns you to yourself is worth keeping: a routine, a room, a person who knew you before the chapter started. Comfort is not a distraction from the ambition. It is what keeps you fit to carry it.

Push shows up inside a chapter that was already pulling. The long period you are living belongs to Rahu, the north node of the Moon, which enlarges what you want and turns you toward what your life has not held before. The long chapter subdivides, and each subdivision, an antardasha, answers to a different lord. Mars takes this one. Wanting now comes with force behind it. Things speed up. A plan that had been circling gets started, a risk that had been hypothetical gets taken, and effort finds an outlet that hunger by itself could not provide. Plenty of people do the boldest work of the chapter in a stretch like this. Competition sharpens too, and rivals can start to feel personal. Friction is built into the pair. Impatience runs high, corners look cuttable, and arguments at work or at home can flare over territory rather than principle. Anger here tends to aim at whatever stands between you and the goal, which makes it useful information and poor company. Physical risk deserves plain mention, as a tendency and nothing more: haste, overreach, and a body asked to keep pace with an ambition. Rest belongs in the equipment list. The upside is real, though. Courage and appetite together cover more ground in a short run than either manages alone, and this is often where the chapter's central move actually happens. You leave it knowing what you will fight for, a shorter and more useful list than what you want.

This is where the chapter announces itself. Rahu, the north lunar node, governs a long period in the Vedic timing system, and the first shorter period inside it, an antardasha, belongs to Rahu as well. The theme arrives undiluted: appetite, reach, and a pull toward whatever your life has not contained so far. Something usually opens. A door appears into a world you had only watched from outside, a place, a field, a set of people, or a version of yourself the old surroundings had no room for. The wanting can feel sudden and complete, as though it had been queued up and waiting. Plans made now tend to run larger than the evidence supports, which is part of how a chapter like this gets its scale. It is also where the care belongs. Appetite of this kind rarely announces when it has had enough, so an opening run can talk you into holding more than you can carry, being dazzled by the shiny version of a thing, or reading speed as progress. None of that is written down in advance. It is a tendency to watch for in yourself. Two things help: arithmetic you have actually done, and friends who will say the unglamorous part out loud. Met with open eyes, this opening run is usually remembered later as the moment the direction changed. The wanting begins here, and so does your education in it.

Wanting picks up a philosophy in this stretch. The chapter you are in answers to Rahu, the Moon's north node. Its current runs toward more: more scope, more novelty, more of whatever you did not grow up with. Inside such a chapter the lords take turns, and a turn like that is an antardasha, a shorter period with a character of its own. Jupiter's brings growth, meaning, and generosity into the picture. Opportunities widen. Teachers, backers, and well-placed people can turn up, and the ambition of the chapter finds more respectable roads to travel. Study tends to be favored, especially study that serves the reaching: a credential, a language, a body of knowledge that gets you into the room. Distant places, higher learning, and matters of law often feature in the older readings of this pair. The common thread is a door opened by someone who knows more than you do. What to watch is the balance between belief and proportion. Jupiter enlarges what it touches, this chapter already enlarges, and together they can sell you scale without foundations: promises past your capacity, a plan built on the best-case column, a conviction that quits listening. That is a pressure rather than a fate, and ordinary arithmetic answers it well. There is also a steadying effect here that people underrate. Ambition with a reason behind it wears better than ambition alone, and this is often the run where the chapter's hunger locates something worth being hungry for.

The chapter's appetite meets the part of life that refuses to hurry. Your long period runs under Rahu, the Moon's north node, a point the older texts describe as never quite satisfied. Within it the texture changes from stretch to stretch, because each stretch, an antardasha, has a lord of its own. Saturn has this one, and Saturn wants proof, patience, and structure, so the pace changes. Results arrive slower than the plan promised. Effort still counts, but it gets repaid on a delay, and the shortcuts that worked earlier in the chapter stop returning much. Obligations gather: the ordinary weight of a job, a household, a debt, an aging body, the people who depend on you. Some of what the chapter built gets tested here, and whatever cannot bear weight tends to show it. That is often felt as frustration, and it reads more usefully as an audit. A goal that survives this stretch is usually worth the rest of the chapter. A goal that quietly collapses had been running on enthusiasm. The moods to watch are discouragement and its opposite number, grinding on without rest, since both can pass for virtue and neither is. Ambition does not end in a run like this. It gets slowed to a speed at which something can actually be built, and the skills and standing you hold afterward tend to be the ones that stay with you.

Cleverness goes to work for the hunger. The chapter around you belongs to Rahu, the Moon's north node, whose taste runs to the new and the unmapped. Every such chapter is broken into antardashas, which is to say into shorter periods, and Mercury takes this one, bringing talk, trade, learning, and quick hands with it. Communication becomes the instrument of ambition. Deals, pitches, applications, negotiations, writing, and introductions all pick up, and this is often where the reach of the era turns into contacts and agreements you can point to. Anything modern or technical suits the pairing: media, software, markets, or a trade you learn on the fly because the opportunity showed up first. Movement increases too, both travel and the daily kind, and the calendar fills. The pitfalls are small print and self-persuasion. Fast talk can outrun the facts, an agreement can get signed in the version of it you wanted to hear, and scattered attention can leave several bright starts unfinished. Reading things twice is unfashionable and effective. It also pays to keep one thread going long enough for it to become a skill rather than an anecdote. With a little discipline applied, this run is where a large appetite acquires a working vocabulary, and where your plans start sounding like something other people can join.
